----------------------Disclaimer---------------------------


Recording phone calls may be subject to complex and varying laws in different countries and jurisdictions. For example, you may need to ensure you have consent from all parties before recording conversations. The developers and contributors are not responsible for any misuse or legal consequences arising from the use of this application.
 You can learn more on Wikipedia at:
 https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telephone_call_recording_laws.


If you are legally required to inform or ask someone for consent before recording, please note that the application DOES NOT handle this for you.
 In some cases, certain features, like automatic call recording, may not be legally allowed. It is your responsibility to ensure compliance with applicable laws. This is not legal advice. Please consult a legal professional for guidance regarding your specific situation.


APPLICATION BEHAVIOR
 Due to the evolving Android ecosystem and varying hardware (OEMs), this software is subject to non-deterministic behavior:

 * Concurrent Calls: The app may fail to detect transitions (e.g., while in a call, a second incoming call arrives, or switching between held calls). In these scenarios, the application may continue to record audio into a single continuous file without separate notifications or new notifications prompts for subsequent callers.

 * Filter Logic Limitations: Due to Android privacy-driven restrictions on real-time phone number access, the app relies on fetching a deprecated value when it receives a phone state updates. We are not aware of other rational workaround for standard apps (alternatives are restrictive or incompatible). This initial check is used to decide whether to automatically record based on your settings. In cases where we receive the value too late, receive invalid data, or receive no data, the application is likely to consider the call as anonymous in its decision process. This should not affect the final file name since we can read the device call logs after the call ended.

 * Unforeseen Failures: Future OS updates, bugs, design choices in the app, or undocumented system behaviors may cause the app to start and/or continue recording, or fail, in a unexpected manner.


USER AWARENESS
 Because deterministic behavior in the application cannot be guaranteed, it is your responsibility to:

 1. Ensure the recording behavior and your application settings aligns with your intent and the specific requirements in your jurisdiction.

 2. Monitor the app behavior on your specific device. If you observe any behavior that does not comply with your local laws, you must immediately cease any activity that constitutes a legal infraction (For example, hanging up the call, deleting the audio files, etc).
I have read the disclaimer and understand the legal requirements, responsibilities, and technical limitations of this software.
We need a few permissions to start recoding. Tap "Grant Access" and approve each item.
Used for recording status and error alerts.
Used to filter known contacts for ignore rules.
Required to detect when a call starts or ends.
Required so we receive the unredacted phone number on phone state events.
Recommended. Keeps recording working away from Wi-Fi, and lets CallVault switch Wireless debugging off after setup. No cable needed.

Keeps the app alive when it needs and allow to bypass possible background startup limitations. On some phones (e.g. OnePlus/OxygenOS) also set this app\'s battery mode to \"Allow background activity\".
Battery exemption set. Now on this App info page, tap \"Battery\", then choose \"Allow background activity\" (Unrestricted) — required so recording survives in the background on OnePlus/OxygenOS.
Select where recordings will be saved.
Required to set up and start the recorder, and it only works on Wi-Fi. Pair once via the notification, then it connects automatically.
Not connected — tap to set up
Recordings older than the selected period are permanently deleted. Checked once a day at the time below.
Recordings older than the selected period will be permanently deleted from your device and/or Google Drive. This can\'t be undone.
Shizuku is running on this phone
CallVault can use it instead, and skip pairing entirely. Or set CallVault up on its own, so it needs nothing else running.
Allow CallVault in Shizuku to finish. Nothing records until you do.
Using Shizuku. There is nothing to pair — setup is done.
Start it from the Shizuku app and come back, and CallVault can use it instead of pairing. Or set CallVault up on its own — it needs nothing else running.
Open Shizuku and start it. It stops whenever the phone restarts, and CallVault cannot record until it is running.
%1$s was not recorded — Shizuku was not running
A call was not recorded — Shizuku was not running
Not available in Shizuku mode — this needs CallVault\'s own recorder.
Stopping the old recorder and starting the new one. This takes a few seconds.
CallVault is recording through Shizuku. VoIP calls, resilient recording and speaker names are not available in this mode.
CallVault is recording with its own recorder. Everything is available, including VoIP calls and speaker names.
The recorder is running. Calls will be recorded.
Shizuku is not installed, so there is nothing to switch to.
Shizuku is not running. Open Shizuku and start it, then try again — it stops whenever the phone restarts.
Shizuku has not allowed CallVault to use it yet. Open Shizuku and allow it, then try again.
Switched, but app-call recording could not be armed. Phone calls will record; app calls may not until you reopen CallVault.
The recorder did not start. Nothing will be recorded until it does.
Shizuku is not installed. CallVault does not need it — this is only for people who already use it.
Shizuku is installed but not running. It has to be started again after every restart of the phone.
Shizuku is running, but has not allowed CallVault to use it yet.
Shizuku is running and ready. With this on, CallVault does not need its own pairing.
Opens Shizuku so you can allow it. Nothing records until you do.
Also record calls made in apps like WhatsApp, Signal and Telegram. Experimental — some apps block recording, and this cannot be known until a call is under way.
Off means CallVault asks first: a notification with a Record button appears when an app call starts.
Tap Record to record this call.
%1$s call. Tap Record to record it.

Recording app calls is more tightly regulated than recording phone calls, and in many places every participant must agree first. Please make sure you are allowed to.\n\nThis is experimental: it works with some apps and not others, and an app can block recording at any time in an update.
CallVault is recording an app call.
An app call was not recorded — CallVault was not ready in time. This can happen for a short while after a phone call ends. The next call should record normally.
An app call was not recorded — the recordings folder is missing or cannot be written to. Choose it again in Settings.
Only your side of that app call was recorded — the other app does not allow its call audio to be captured.
Couldn\'t enable on this device — VoIP recording isn\'t available here.
Contact names come from the calling app\'s own call notification. If notifications are turned off for that app, its recordings are saved without a name.
Recommended. Keeps recording working when you leave Wi-Fi, and lets CallVault switch Wireless debugging off. No cable needed.
Without this, recording only works on Wi-Fi, and Wireless debugging has to stay on.
CallVault can keep Wireless debugging off. If you turn this off, recording stops for a few seconds while CallVault restarts it over Wi-Fi — and away from Wi-Fi it can\'t restart.
Leave USB debugging on while you use Shizuku. Shizuku\'s service is started over Android\'s debugging service and stops when it does — CallVault does not need this switch in Shizuku mode.
Couldn\'t change it — CallVault needs the permission it gets during setup.
Wireless debugging has to stay on because USB debugging is off. Turn on USB debugging in Settings ▸ Experimental and CallVault will switch Wireless debugging off again.
Record calls via a background privileged service so Wireless debugging can stay off between calls. Experimental.
Turn off Wireless debugging when idle
Disable Wireless debugging once the recorder service is connected; re-enabled briefly only when needed.
Pick a folder (in the Google Drive app) to copy recordings to.
Cloud folders (like Google Drive) can\'t be used for recording. Pick on-device storage — use the Google Drive backup option for cloud copies.
⚠ This recording folder is in the cloud, which is unreliable for capture. Choose an on-device folder.
Record calls even when there is no Wi-Fi network. Needs USB debugging on.
Keep a recording going even if the background helper is killed mid-call (e.g. when you lock the screen). Experimental.
"Charging only" keeps recording alive if you lock the screen during a call. Other modes let USB transfer data but can interrupt a recording when you lock the phone.
Leave this alone while you use Shizuku. Changing it restarts Android\'s debugging service, and Shizuku stops with it — you would have to start Shizuku again before the next call could be recorded.
Not changed: a recording is in progress. Changing this restarts Android\'s debugging service, which would end the recording.

This opens a local debugging port on your phone so calls can record with no Wi-Fi. It is protected by your device\'s key, but it is a small security tradeoff. Only enable it if you need to record calls without Wi-Fi.
Indicates if the call is cross-country (true/false)
Off: phone calls are ignored completely — no recording, no notification. App calls are unaffected.
If you have difficulties, try AAC, it is widely supported by OEMs.
Microphone audio source tuned for voice communications. Built-in echo cancellation.
Captures audio directly from the device main microphone. Minor noise reduction.
Records both sides of a phone calls. The raw audio, with phone tones.
Capture audio from other apps, except those that restrict recording (respects app opt-out flags).
Captures the final, combined audio exactly as it is sent to your speakers.
Captures raw, natural microphone audio without any automatic filtering or enhancement.
Tuned for video recording, focusing on audio from the direction of the camera.
Microphone with processing tuned for speech recognition (reduced noise).
Records only your side of a phone call (uplink).
Records only the other person side of a phone call (downlink).
High-speed microphone mode designed for live music and real-time audio apps.
To report a bug, enable this, reproduce the issue, then turn it off and share the logs.
Debug logging is ON. Remember to turn it off when you\'re done to save space.
Logs from your last debug session are ready to share.
No logs yet. Enable debug logging, reproduce the issue, then tap share.
Tap to open CallVault and turn it off when you\'re done.
CallVault is a fork of ShizuCallRecorder
Buy me a coffee on Ko-fi
Selected output folder is missing, invalid, or we do not have permission to write to it. Select one in the app settings.
Scrcpy-server binary is missing or the security SHA256 check failed. This should not happen, please report this.
Failed to create recording file. Please check the storage permissions and/or select a new recording folder in the app settings.
Failed to start the recording. An error occurred when calling the ShellService binder method.
The recording is empty — no audio was captured. Open Shizuku and check it is still running; it stops whenever the phone restarts.
The recording is empty — no audio was captured because the recorder daemon was not running. Check that Developer options and Wireless debugging are enabled.
The recorder daemon stopped — this call is NOT being recorded. Check that Developer options and Wireless debugging are enabled.
Recording did not start — try a different audio format in Settings
A recording could not be copied to your cloud folder. It is still saved on this device — check the folder in Settings.
An unexpected error occurred during recording. Please report this with the steps to reproduce and the apps logs.
Choose where your recordings are stored. You can change this later in Settings.
With Google Drive, the copy on this device is temporary and is deleted after it has been uploaded.
Choose how often recordings are uploaded to your Google Drive folder.
Every call is uploaded automatically as soon as it finishes.
Choose which calls are recorded automatically. You can fine-tune this later in Settings.
With both phone calls and app calls off, CallVault will not record anything. Turn at least one on unless that is what you want.
A feature still being proven. It is off by default — you can turn it on later in Settings.
CallVault is not on an app store, so it checks GitHub for new versions itself.
Two optional settings that keep recording working in tricky conditions. You can skip these and change them later in Settings.
Keep recording when the screen locks

On some phones, locking the screen during a call can stop the recording. Setting USB to \"Charging only\" prevents that. (Your phone then defaults to charging when plugged into a PC — pick File transfer manually when you need it.)
USB is set to Charging only

CallVault can turn a recording into text on the phone itself, and write a short summary from it — nothing is sent anywhere. Choose when that happens, which language your calls are in, and download what it needs.
Set to the language this phone is set to. Naming it is far more reliable than letting the app guess, and you can still pick a different one per call later.
Transcribing needs a speech model on the phone first: %1$s is %2$d MB, %3$s is %4$d MB. Transcribing a call then takes roughly the length of the call and works the processor hard.
Transcribing needs a speech model on the phone first: %1$s. Transcribing a call then takes roughly the length of the call and works the processor hard.
Once a call has a transcript, CallVault can also write a short summary of it — on the phone, like everything else here.
Both downloads only run over Wi-Fi, and they keep going in the background. You can carry on and finish setup now — Settings ▸ Transcription & summaries shows the same progress afterwards.
Pick the recording format and bit rate. Opus at 16 kbps is recommended for clear voice at small file sizes.
Choose how saved recordings are named.
You\'re all set. CallVault is ready to record your calls.
Open Settings to choose where recordings are saved.
Finish Wireless Debugging pairing in setup.
CallVault records through Wireless debugging, which needs Developer options. Recording cannot work until you re-enable Developer options (and Wireless debugging) in system settings.
An update removed a permission CallVault needs to restart recording. It may still work for now — tap here, then turn Wireless debugging on once to restore it. No reinstall needed.
CallVault records calls automatically per your settings.
This recording is saved on this device and in Drive.
Once a day, look for a new version on GitHub.
I build CallVault on my own, in my free time — free, open source, no ads, no tracking. ☕ If it\'s useful to you, a small tip keeps me going. Either way, thanks! 🙏
Some are saved both on this device and in Drive.
%1$s will be kept — only in Drive.
%1$s will be kept — only on this device.
Includes the setup journal, which is always kept from the first run. Tap to read it.
Tap to read the most recent entries.
The entries collected so far are removed. If logging is still on, a new log starts immediately.

A call takes roughly its own length to transcribe, and uses every core of your phone while it does. Expect it to get warm and to use noticeable battery.\n\nYou can stop a run at any time from the badge beside the title.
Transcribing uses the processor heavily and will drain the battery.
Your phone may get warm while this runs.
Not enough free space. Free some up and try again.
The download was damaged and has been discarded. Try again.
The download did not finish. Try again.
Not enough free space. Free some up and try again.
The download was damaged and has been discarded. Try again.
The download did not finish. Try again.

Summaries are written on your phone — nothing is sent anywhere. That costs a %1$.1f GB download and about %2$.1f GB of memory while it runs, so it needs a recent phone with room to spare. A short call takes a minute or two.
The summariser is Google\'s Gemma 4, used under the Apache 2.0 licence. It is downloaded separately rather than included in CallVault.
Written on your phone, about a minute or two
Transcribe this call first — the summary is written from the transcript.
Waiting for the transcript to finish.
This transcript has no words in it, so there is nothing to summarise.
Download the summariser in Settings first.
Waiting for the transcription to finish — they cannot share the phone.
That did not produce a usable summary. You can try again.
%1$.1f GB to download, over Wi-Fi only
About %1$.1f GB of memory while it runs
Roughly a minute or two for a short call, longer for a long one
Everything happens on your phone. Nothing is sent anywhere.
It needs a recent phone with room to spare. On an older one it may be slow or fail.
Show what the summariser costs before downloading it
This frees %1$.1f GB. Summaries you have already written are kept, but you will need to download it again to write any more.
This throws away the %1$.1f GB already downloaded. Starting again would fetch all of it from the beginning.

Detection is unreliable for languages that are not written in Latin letters — Hebrew, Arabic, Russian and Chinese often come back spelled out in English letters, or as one long block of text. Name the language if you can.
Transcripts are made only when you ask for one, from the button on a recording.
Each call is transcribed as soon as it ends. Older calls are left alone — transcribe those from the button on a recording.
Calls that have no transcript yet are transcribed at the chosen time. A 30-minute call takes about 30 minutes.
The first one may take a while
Transcribing %1$s keeps your phone busy and uses noticeable battery. You can stop it at any time.\n\nThis question can be turned back on under Transcription in Settings.
Choose the language per recording instead of always using the one above. It applies to that recording only.
Shows how long it will take and lets you cancel.
No speech was recognised in this recording.

This call is about %1$d minutes long. CallVault can only transcribe recordings up to %2$d minutes on the device for now — longer ones would run out of memory partway through. The recording itself is safe.
Transcribing happens on this phone, so it needs a speech model downloaded first. You can choose and download one in Settings.
Type a word to search across every transcript you have.
No call contains those words. Only whole words match, so try another form of the word.
The transcript of %1$s will be deleted. The recording itself is kept, and you can transcribe it again later.
CallVault keeps failing to restart its recorder, so calls are not being recorded. Reopening the app usually clears it.
Ask for your screen lock before showing recordings and transcripts. Also keeps them out of screenshots and the app switcher.
Set a screen lock on your phone to use this.
Renaming changes this tag on every recording that has it. Renaming it to a tag that already exists merges the two.
A misdial or a call that rang out is deleted the moment it ends, before it is transcribed or uploaded. Nothing already recorded is affected.

Once your recordings pass this, the daily clean-up deletes the oldest from this phone until they fit. Starred recordings are never deleted, even if that means going over. A recording kept in Drive as well only loses its copy here.
Recordings will be deleted from this phone whenever they exceed the limit, oldest first. Starred recordings are never taken. This cannot be undone.
Calls will not be recorded until this phone joins a Wi-Fi network once. Any network will do and it does not need internet — a few seconds is enough, then it keeps working even off Wi-Fi.
Copying to Google Drive stopped some time ago. Nothing is lost — the recordings are still on this phone — but they are not backed up. Open CallVault to check your storage settings.
Calls will not be recorded until Shizuku is running again. A reboot stops it, so it has to be started once after the phone restarts.

After a restart this stops working until the phone joins a Wi-Fi network once. Any network will do and it does not need internet — a few seconds is enough. CallVault will tell you when that is needed.
Save a small .json beside each recording
Uses the same format as BCR, so apps built for it — such as bcr-gui — can read your recordings\' details. Only worth turning on if you use one.
Mark a moment to find it later, or stop recording.
Switch an app off and its calls are never recorded. Everything is on until you change it. Apps that cannot record audio are not listed, since they cannot place the kind of call this captures.
Paused. Nothing is being saved right now.
Held for a phone call. This recording will continue when you return.
You\'re not on Wi-Fi, so CallVault will have no way to reach the recorder. Calls won\'t be recorded until you connect to Wi-Fi or turn this back on.
Off-Wi-Fi recording needs USB debugging. With it off, calls made away from Wi-Fi won\'t be recorded.
Keep Wireless debugging on for recording

If you switch Wireless debugging off while nothing else lets CallVault in, it turns it back on so calls keep recording. When this is off, your switch stays off and the notification says recording is paused.
